The '''1966 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 80th staging of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]'s premier inter-county hurling tournament. The championship ran from 15 May 1966 to 4 September 1966.

[[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] entered the championship as the [[1965 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|defending champions]], however, they were beaten by [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] in the [[#Munster quarter-finals|Munster quarter-finals]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tipperarylive.ie/news/sport/553436/tipperary-s-hurlers-were-up-for-every-dance-in-the-60-s.html|title=Tipperary's hurlers were up for every dance in the '60's|publisher=Tipperary Live|date=25 June 2020|access-date=21 February 2025|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/then---now---tom-aherne/657270/then-now-hurling-great-eamonn-grimes.html|title=Then & Now: Limerick hurling great Eamonn Grimes|publisher=Limerick Live|date=19 August 2021|access-date=21 February 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

The [[1966 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|All-Ireland final]] was played on 4 September 1996 at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]], between [[Cork GAA|Cork]] and [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]], in what was their 14th meeting in the final overall and a first meeting in the final in [[1947 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|19 years]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kilkennypeople.ie/news/gaelic-games/52616/Hurling-stalwarts-remembered-.html|title=Hurling stalwarts remembered|publisher=Kilkenny People|date=5 April 2013|access-date=21 February 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> Cork won the match by 3–09 to 1–10 to claim their 20th All-Ireland title overall and a first title in [[1954 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|12 years]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20419245.html|title=The mission accomplished to end Cork famine in 1966|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=3 September 2016|access-date=21 February 2025|first=Michael|last=Moynihan}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/regionals/cork/sport/gaa/corks-route-to-66-all-ireland-hurling-title-gives-hope-for-ending-latest-famine/39221937.html|title=Cork's route to '66 All-Ireland hurling title gives hope for ending latest famine|publisher=The Corkman|date=23 May 2020|access-date=21 February 2025|first=Noel|last=Horgan}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport-columnists/arid-41067812.html|title=Paul Rouse: History weighs on Cork shoulders but expectation survives|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=10 February 2023|access-date=21 February 2025|first=Paul|last=Rouse}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/news/the-66-all-ireland-will-always-carry-special-memories/27081031.html|title=The '66 All Ireland will always carry special memories|publisher=The Corkman|date=11 November 2010|access-date=21 February 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

Cork's [[Seánie Barry]] was the championship's [[#Top scorers|top scorer]] with 3–23. Cork's [[Justin McCarthy (hurler)|Justin McCarthy]] was the choice for [[Texaco Hurler of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40362959.html|title=PM O'Sullivan meets Justin McCarthy: The Cork hurler who was every boy’s hero|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=20 August 2023|access-date=21 February 2025|first=PM|last=O'Sullivan}}</ref>

==Championship statistics==

===Miscellaneous===

* [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]]'s defeat by [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] in the first round of the Munster championship was the team's first defeat since the provincial decider of 1963.  It also put an end to Tipperary's hopes of capturing a third All-Ireland title in-a-row.
* Prior to the Munster semi-final between [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] and [[Cork GAA|Cork]] there was a minute's silence in memory of Dr. Rogers, [[Bishop of Killaloe]], who died the previous day.
* In the Leinster semi-final [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]]'s [[Willie Murphy (Wexford hurler)|Willie Murphy]] scores a remarkable own-goal for [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]].
